courses.title: Learn Vue 3: Step by Step
courses.description:
Go from your very first Vue template to components, composables and state management with Pinia.

Vue is one of the most approachable JavaScript frameworks, and Vue 3 makes it even more powerful. In this series we start with nothing more than a script tag and build up, one idea at a time, to a real application structure.

Each episode is short and focused. We pause to discuss the mistakes beginners usually make, and the "little confusing things" that rarely get explained, so you understand why Vue behaves the way it does.

By the end you will be comfortable building components, sharing state between them, and organising a Vue project with modern tooling.

## What you'll learn

• Create reactive Vue 3 applications and bind data, attributes and events
• Render lists and conditionals, and use computed properties
• Build reusable components and pass data with props and events
• Handle forms with v-model and communicate between parent and child components
• Use slots to create flexible components
• Set up a project with Vite and the script setup syntax
• Extract logic into composables and share data with provide/inject
• Manage application state with Pinia

## Requirements

• Basic HTML, CSS and JavaScript
• A code editor and a modern browser
• Node.js installed for the later episodes

## Who this course is for

• Beginners who know some JavaScript and want to learn Vue
• Developers moving from jQuery or other frameworks
• Laravel developers who want a modern front end

## Course details

**Instructor:** Laracasts
**Video source:** YouTube playlist "Learn Vue 3: Step By Step" by Laracasts
**Video language:** English, can be dubbed into many languages
**Content:** 27 lessons · about 4.7 hours

lessons.title: The Absolute Basics
lessons.description: Let's start...at the beginning! We'll pull in Vue 3 through a CDN, and then review the absolute basics of the framework, including Vue initialization, text interpolation, and reactivity.

lessons.title: Attribute Binding and Event Handling
lessons.description: You'll often want to bind the value of an HTML attribute to an expression. We can allow for this by using the v-bind directive. As part of this lesson, we'll also get a first taste of event handling in Vue.

lessons.title: Lists, Conditionals, and Computed Properties
lessons.description: Let's dig into a few more important concepts in this episode. Using the example of an assignment list, we'll learn how to loop over arrays, conditionally display HTML, and prepare computed properties.

lessons.title: Your First Vue Component
lessons.description: We've now learned the absolute basics of Vue; however, this still looks nothing like real-life Vue applications. Let's begin digging into custom Vue components.

lessons.title: One Vue Component Per File
lessons.description: We can technically inline child Vue components, but you'll rarely do so. Instead, a much cleaner approach is to store each Vue component within its own file. Let's take care of that in this episode.

lessons.title: Component Props
lessons.description: If we want our Vue components to be as flexible as possible, we should figure out a way to pass in data from the outside. This way, each "instance" of a component can be configurable. Props allow for this!

lessons.title: Bring it All Together
lessons.description: Let's now return to the simple assignment lists that we worked on in episode three. But this time, we'll approach it with fresh eyes and a new understanding of how Vue components work.

lessons.title: Handle a Form Submission
lessons.description: In this episode, we'll combine forms and events to allow a user to create new assignments on the fly.

lessons.title: Parent-Child State Communication
lessons.description: Now, let's throw a wrench into the mix. If we extract a new Vue component, we'll then need to figure out how our components should communicate state changes.

lessons.title: It's All So Easy
lessons.description: Once you understand the basics of Vue, you'll quickly find that things, which were incredibly time consuming years ago, can now be accomplished in seconds. Let's review a couple examples in this video.

lessons.title: Component Responsibility
lessons.description: In this episode, we'll discuss component responsibility as we refactor to an AssignmentsTags component. I think of component responsibility in the same way that I think of server-side class responsibility. "Does this bit of logic belong here?"

lessons.title: A Deeper Look at v-model
lessons.description: We reviewed the basics of the v-model directive at the beginning of the series, but I think it's time that we take a deeper look. What exactly happens when we apply v-model to an input? And can we also use it on custom Vue components?

lessons.title: Lifecycle Hooks, Fake APIs, and AJAX
lessons.description: So far, we've been hard-coding the list of assignments directly within our Vue component. But of course, that's not overly realistic. Let's switch over to using the fetch() JavaScript API to request data from a fake API.

lessons.title: Flexible Vue Components With Slots and Flags
lessons.description: There are many ways to allow for more flexible and configurable components. Let's begin with two simple and obvious techniques: slots and flags.

lessons.title: Named Slots
lessons.description: So far, we've been working with components that only required a single, default slot. But, of course in real life, you'll encounter situations where you need to insert content in multiple areas. In these cases, we can used named slots.

lessons.title: An Introduction to Vite
lessons.description: Great job, if you've made it this far. I think you're now ready to move on to part two of this series. Now that you understand many of the fundamentals of Vue, let's now figure out how to actually construct a single-page application using it.

lessons.title: Little Confusing Things About Vue
lessons.description: At this stage, I fully expect you to be confused in numerous ways. We went from building basic Vue components to scaffolding a full single-page application with routing, configuration, aliases, and more.

lessons.title: Two Mental Leaps to Script Setup
lessons.description: I must admit, I feel bad for what I'm about to do. You were becoming so comfortable, and I had to suddenly throw a wrench into the gears. In this lesson, let's mentally adjust to working with the Composition API and script setup.

lessons.title: From Mixins to Composables
lessons.description: Let's talk about code re-use in this episode. We'll begin by reviewing a basic example using a traditional, mixin-based approach. And then, we'll convert it to the more recommended approach these days: composables.

lessons.title: Composables Example
lessons.description: Let's review another example of a composable. This time, we'll leverage localStorage and Vue reactivity to "remember" a form input's value - even if you refresh the page.

lessons.description: In this lesson: Refactoring to defineEmits and defineProps. Part of the "Tooling and the Composition API" section of Learn Vue 3: Step by Step.

courses.title: Angular Tutorial for Beginners
courses.description:
Learn Angular from the ground up, from components and data binding to services, routing and forms.

Angular is a complete platform for building large, maintainable web applications. This course introduces the framework one concept at a time, with a small, runnable example in every lesson.

You will start with components and templates, move on to directives, services and HTTP, and finish with two complete series on template-driven and reactive forms.

The lessons are short, so you can follow the whole path or jump straight to the topic you need.

## What you'll learn

• Create an Angular project and understand its structure
• Build components and use interpolation, property, class, style and event binding
• Control templates with ngIf, ngSwitch and ngFor
• Share data between components and format output with pipes
• Use services and dependency injection
• Fetch data over HTTP with observables and handle errors
• Configure routing, route parameters and child routes
• Build and validate template-driven and reactive forms

## Requirements

• Basic HTML, CSS and JavaScript
• Some familiarity with TypeScript is helpful
• Node.js and a code editor installed

## Who this course is for

• Beginners starting with Angular
• Front-end developers moving from other frameworks
• Students building a single-page application project

courses.title: Laravel 11 for Beginners
courses.description:
Build web applications with Laravel, the popular PHP framework, from the ground up.

Laravel is one of the most loved PHP frameworks, with an elegant syntax and everything you need to build modern web applications. In this series we build one up step by step, starting with routes and views.

You will learn how Laravel structures an application, how to work with a database through migrations and Eloquent, and how to handle forms, validation and deletion.

Every lesson adds a small feature, so you finish with a working application and a clear mental model of the framework.

## What you'll learn

• Install Laravel and understand its project structure
• Define routes, wildcards and named routes
• Create views with Blade directives, layouts, slots and components
• Style your pages with CSS and Tailwind
• Design a database with migrations, models, factories and seeders
• Organise code with the MVC pattern and controllers
• Model relationships with foreign keys
• Build forms with validation, flash messages and delete requests

## Requirements

• Basic PHP and HTML knowledge
• PHP and Composer installed (covered in the first lesson)
• A code editor

## Who this course is for

• PHP developers new to Laravel
• Beginners who want to build database-driven websites
• Students preparing a back-end project

courses.title: MERN Stack CRUD Application
courses.description:
Build a complete full-stack CRUD application with MongoDB, Express, React and Node.js, and deploy it.

The MERN stack lets you build an entire web application in JavaScript. In this series we build a user-management app from an empty folder to a deployed project.

First we create the REST API with Express and MongoDB, then a React front end with routing and forms, and finally we connect the two and ship the result.

It is a compact, project-based way to see how every layer of a modern full-stack app fits together.

## What you'll learn

• Set up an Express server and connect it to MongoDB
• Create REST endpoints for creating, reading, updating and deleting data
• Structure a back-end project with routes, controllers and models
• Create a React app with a Bootstrap-styled data table
• Navigate between pages with React Router
• Send and receive data with Axios
• Give users feedback with toast notifications
• Deploy the app with Render, Vercel and MongoDB Atlas

## Requirements

• JavaScript fundamentals
• Basic React knowledge
• Node.js installed

## Who this course is for

• Developers who know React and want to build full-stack apps
• Students looking for a MERN project for their portfolio
• Anyone who wants to learn CRUD end to end

## Course details

courses.title: Bootstrap 5 Tutorial
courses.description:
Create responsive, good-looking pages quickly with Bootstrap 5 and build a complete landing page.

Bootstrap remains one of the fastest ways to build responsive websites. This course covers everything new in Bootstrap 5 and walks you through the components you will use most.

We design a responsive landing page as we go, so every lesson ends with something you can see in the browser.

You will also learn how to customise Bootstrap so your site does not look like every other Bootstrap site.

## What you'll learn

• Set up Bootstrap 5 and understand what is new
• Style text, colours and buttons with utility classes
• Create responsive layouts with containers and the grid
• Build navbars, cards, accordions and list groups
• Create and validate forms
• Use tooltips, modals, offcanvas panels, dropdowns and tabs
• Add icons to your pages
• Customise Bootstrap with your own styles

## Requirements

• Basic HTML and CSS
• A code editor and a browser
• No Bootstrap experience needed

## Who this course is for

• Beginners who want to build responsive pages fast
• Designers who want to turn layouts into code
• Developers who need a quick UI toolkit for projects

## Course details

**Instructor:** The Net Ninja
**Video source:** YouTube playlist "Bootstrap 5 Tutorial" by The Net Ninja
**Video language:** English, can be dubbed into many languages
**Content:** 20 lessons · about 2.9 hours
